newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts downward.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts downward.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps drifted downward in quiet trading at midday Wednesday as the market wound down ahead of the Lunar New Year and Haj holidays, traders said.
"The market is very quiet in the absence of any new indicators. Most people are winding down for the holidays," one broker said.
Front month February gas oil swaps were last quoted down around 20 cents from Tuesday at $25.05/$25.20 per barrel, brokers said. March was last quoted largely unchanged at $25.75/$25.95 per barrel.

Traders said the lower prices were in part due to falls to futures prices on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) where February gas oil closed down $1.00 per tonne to $203.00 while March crude lost 11 cents to end at $22.43 per barrel on Tuesday.
They also said the continued offer of physical cargoes at below $25.00 per barrel free-on-board Singapore is weighing heavily on the market.
On Tuesday one 150,000-barrel cargo traded at $24.80 per barrel fob Singapore.

Jet fuel was unchanged at the higher levels reflecting the tight prompt supplies and strong regional buying interest. The February jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade was last quoted $4.40/$4.80 per barrel.

On the physical market premiums remain strong with a cargo sold on Monday to China at $2.05 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight basis, up 20 cents from the previous traded level.
Fuel oil swaps were quoted slightly lower at $97.50/$99.25 per tonne in quiet trading, down 25 cents from Tuesday.
